Seven studios compete for Melbourne's dance students. None has finished the work AI search now rewards.

We audited 7 dance and ballroom studios serving the Melbourne market head to head: site quality, Google's local results, and 6 live checks across ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI. The sites range from 49 to 86. The AI engines name only six of the 7. The field averages 62 (D) on AI readiness, 7 of 7 have no FAQ or Q&A structured data, and 6 of 7 have no llms.txt file. Whichever studio closes that gap first changes the answer for everyone searching this market.

Prepared by SiteTradeIn · Market snapshot generated 29 Oct 2026 · Independent audit — not commissioned by any studio in the field · See the ranked list

About this report

This is a market-wide snapshot, not an audit of a single business. We picked one competitive local market — dance and ballroom instruction in the Melbourne, FL area — and ran the same measurement against every studio that competes for it: an automated site-quality grade across seven categories, where each studio shows up in Google's local results, and 6 live checks asking three AI engines who they'd recommend for two real buyer queries. Every studio named below is graded on identical criteria, on the same day, with no advance notice.

The point isn't to single any one studio out — it's to show what an AI-search-era competitive landscape actually looks like once you measure it instead of guessing at it. If your studio is one of the 7 below, this is where you stand today.

What the field shows

  • Arthur Murray Dance Studio Melbourne (86) and Infinity Ballroom Dance (76) lead on site quality, and the field runs down to 49.
  • No studio earns an A for AI readiness. The field averages 62 (D) on the category that decides whether an AI engine can read, trust and quote a site; the best score in the market is 85.
  • None of the 7 studios has FAQ or Q&A structured data, and 6 have no llms.txt file — the two cheapest AI-answer signals available. No studio in the market has both.
  • Two of the 7 are franchise locations (one Fred Astaire and one Arthur Murray); the rest are independent studios.
  • The gap between #1 and #7 is 37 points on identical criteria. Nothing in the scorecard requires a rebuild or a rebrand to close it — just the work.

One of the 7 studios is never named on any of the 6 checks: Tango & Ties. For a studio not doing this work, that's the default outcome — not a penalty, just the result of nobody in that seat having claimed it yet.

What separates the winners from the rest

  • Off-site proof, not just on-site polish. AI answers draw on what other sites say about a studio, not just on its own pages, so reviews, directory listings and a complete Google profile carry real weight.
  • Being unmistakably “in Melbourne.” Studios that serve Melbourne from nearby towns need pages, profiles and listings that say so in the words people search.
  • A complete, specific site. The strongest sites have no missing H1s or meta descriptions, alt text on their images, and schema that describes what the studio actually is.
  • Content matched to how people actually ask. The broad question and the ballroom question pull from different result sets — a studio needs to answer both.

Every monthRe-measure all 3 engines, both queries, and the mapAI answers shift; a competitor closing this gap first changes the answer for everyone else.

Methodology & notes

Field (7 studios): arthurmurraymelbournefl.com, infinityballroomdance.com, fredastaire.com/west-melbourne, melbourneballroom.com, dancindance.com, tangoandties.com, sundanceballroom.com. Chosen from live Google searches on 29 Oct 2026: every adult ballroom, Latin or partner-dance studio with a working website that appeared in Google's local results for Melbourne dance searches. Salsa Heat's Melbourne class is ranked with Salsa Heat on the Orlando page. Google's Melbourne searches also mixed in a few listings from Melbourne, Australia; they aren't counted. Left out: The Apollo Ballroom (no website of its own, though ChatGPT names it), Hip Motions (a belly dance studio), Bliss Fitness Studio (a fitness studio), and the youth, ballet and competition studios that lead the broad answers (The Dance Zone, Brevard Ballet Academy, Ultimate Dance Florida, Dance Mania All Stars, Turning Pointe, Heather's Dance Studio).

Site audit: the same SiteTradeIn engine run for every studio on 29 Oct 2026, up to six pages per site, seven categories. Franchise locations that live on a national website (Fred Astaire) share that site's robots.txt, llms.txt, sitemap and templates.

AI visibility: 6 live checks — ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI, each asked “What are the best dance studios in Melbourne, FL?” and “What are the best ballroom dance studios in Melbourne, FL?” with a request for a top-five numbered list. Rankings are taken from each engine's own list; presence was confirmed by reading the raw response text, and every franchise mention was matched to its location. Each question was asked in a fresh session of each engine's web app (ChatGPT and Gemini logged out, Google's AI Mode), not through a developer API.

Google: local (Places) and first-page organic results captured in a live browser session on 29 Oct 2026 for “ballroom dance lessons melbourne fl”; “dance lessons melbourne fl”; “salsa lessons melbourne fl”; “wedding dance lessons melbourne fl”; “ballroom dance lessons palm bay fl”, plus the organic searches “best dance studios in melbourne fl” and “ballroom dance studio melbourne”. Each query named the city; results vary by searcher location and over time.

Independence. This report is a market-wide measurement, not commissioned by or customized for any single studio named in it.

Limits. AI answers and search results vary between runs and over time; these are a point-in-time sample, not a fixed ranking.
